_comment: Shared parity table for the block control allow-list matcher. PHP runs every case through ControlCatalog::allowed(); JS runs the same cases through includesControl() in resources/framework/inspector/Inspector.tsx. The rule lived only in JS until the REST surface gained the ability to write the style tree, and a server that disagreed with the editor about what a block allows is the bug this table exists to prevent.

cases.why: a glob covers every id under its prefix
exact ids and globs coexist in one list
an exact id grants only itself, not its siblings
a glob grants nothing outside its own prefix
the split is on the FIRST dot, so a glob also covers deeper ids
a bare wildcard is not a wildcard — nothing opts a block into every control
an id with no dot can only match exactly
a dotless id is its own prefix, so a glob does grant it (an artifact of the shared rule, unreachable while every control id has a dot)
a bare prefix does not act as a glob
matching is exact, never a string prefix
matching is case-sensitive on the glob side
matching is case-sensitive on the id side
